messages:
maria-support: FYI customer Streamly reporting big p95 spikes on chat generation since ~13:10 UTC. They see 2-3x latency on their /v1/chat endpoint. link to convo: https://zendesk/streamly/789

liam-eng: Thanks. Any idea if this is across models or a single route?

maria-support: It's the hosted route `streamly-chat-prod` pinned to `redwood/opt-chat-3b` (quantized). Only started after midday. They said throughput is same but tail latency increased.

charlie-eng: @liam could be batching changes or kernel selection. I'll check recent deploys.

deploy-bot: deploy finished: service=runtime-worker image=runtime@sha256:aa12  timestamp=1778999800  env=prod region=us-west-2

liam-eng: Can someone pull p95 by model & node from console for 12:30-13:45? Need p50/p95/p99 + inflight queue depth.

ops-bot: Query run: metrics/p95_by_model from 2026-03-19T12:00 to 2026-03-19T14:30. Results: redwood/opt-chat-3b p95 jumped from 180ms -> 520ms around 13:08. inflight_queue depth +12 on workers serving streamly-route.

dana-support: Customer logs attached: 
```
2026-03-19T13:10:14Z INFO request_id=abc123 start seq_len=512
2026-03-19T13:10:14Z INFO request_id=abc123 end tokens=64 duration_ms=620
```

charlie-eng: That duration matches p95. Two quick hypotheses: autoscaler lag (burst) or a kernel fallback triggered for long seqs. Also need to check KV cache evictions.

liam-eng: Replayed a subset of traffic locally against same model/quant config: saw a small percent of calls hitting slower kernel path when batch size > 8. Customer traffic shows bursty batching pattern.

maria-support: Customer is on dedicated pool with reserved capacity. They said they didn't change traffic. They did increase parallel sessions by a third at 12:45 though.

charlie-eng: Ok — likely batching + a recent runtime change that altered batching thresholds. Rolling diff in prod?

liam-eng: I just found runtime change in PR #4218 that adjusted batching window from 12ms -> 25ms to optimize throughput. Deployed at 1778999800. That matches timing.

tom-pm: We need to decide prioritization. Customer impact looks high (SLA p95). Recommend immediate rollback of batching change for dedicated pools, then include safer rollout checks in backlog.

charlie-eng: Agreed. Proposed mitigation: revert batching window for dedicated pools only, and enable per-customer max_batch_size override. Can do canary to 10% first.

liam-eng: I'll run a quick canary revert on a single worker group and monitor p95. If it drops, escalate rollback across the cluster.

ops-bot: Action created: INC-2026-183 Streamly p95 regression. Priority=P1. Owner=liam-eng.

maria-support: Notifying customer: "we're investigating and may temporarily adjust server settings to restore latency. Will update in 30m"

liam-eng: Canary revert started. Command: `kubectl set image deploy/runtime-worker runtime=runtime@sha256:aa11` (previous image).

charlie-eng: Monitoring dashboards now. Also adding a quick metric to track kernel-fallback-rate and batch-size-distribution per route.

ops-bot: Metric alarm: streamly-route p95 > 400ms triggered at 13:12 UTC. Alert sent to oncall.

liam-eng: Canary looks good after revert, p95 down to ~190ms on group-a. I'll schedule rollout to remaining groups over next 20m.

tom-pm: After we stabilize, we should add to product backlog: acceptance criteria for batching change: A) no p95 regression >10% for pinned dedicated routes in 30m post-deploy; B) automatic per-customer override when latency >X; C) rollout gated by canary with traffic-mirroring.

charlie-eng: I'll create a backlog ticket with those ACs and link INC-2026-183.

maria-support: Customer updated: "we saw improvement after your change, thanks. Please follow up on permanent fix."

liam-eng: Rolling update complete. p95 stable. Assigning deeper RCA to charlie-eng + liam-eng for root cause + postmortem. ETA for RCA doc: EOD tomorrow.

tom-pm: Thanks team. Make sure we prioritize the product work (batching rollout controls) next sprint. I'll allocate PM resources. :thumbsup:

charlie-eng: Filing backlog ticket now: PROD-7234 "Guarded batching rollout + per-customer overrides". Adding acceptance criteria + test plan.

maria-support: Closing loop with customer and marking incident as acknowledged.

liam-eng: Leaving notes in the incident: `cause: batching window widened in PR #4218; effect: increased batch sizes during bursts -> kernel fallback; mitigation: revert and staged rollout; next: per-customer override + canary gating.`

maria-support: Thanks all :heart:
